questions.question: The SDLC model combining iterative development with waterfall structure for large projects.
questions.explanation: RUP is an iterative framework that organizes development into four phases while incorporating best practices from various methodologies.

questions.question: The process of ensuring software continues to work correctly after changes are made.
questions.explanation: Regression testing verifies that recent code changes haven't adversely affected existing functionality.

questions.question: The principle stating each SDLC phase should produce specific deliverables.
questions.explanation: Phase gates require specific criteria and deliverables to be met before proceeding to the next phase.

questions.question: The type of prototyping where the prototype is discarded after requirements are finalized.
questions.explanation: Throwaway prototyping builds a quick model to clarify requirements, which is then discarded before building the actual system.

questions.question: The type of prototyping where the prototype evolves into the final system.
questions.explanation: Evolutionary prototyping continuously refines the prototype, eventually transforming it into the production system.

questions.question: The maintenance type that improves code structure without changing functionality.
questions.explanation: Preventive maintenance restructures code to prevent future problems and improve maintainability without altering behavior.

questions.question: The metric measuring the effort required to understand and modify code.
questions.explanation: Maintainability Index quantifies how easily software can be maintained based on factors like complexity and documentation.

questions.question: The formal review process where code is examined before integration.
questions.explanation: Code inspection is a systematic peer review technique to detect defects early through structured examination.

questions.question: The document describing how the system will be built from a technical perspective.
questions.explanation: SDD details the technical architecture, components, interfaces, and data design for implementing the system.

questions.question: The approach where critical system features are identified and developed first.
questions.explanation: Risk-driven development prioritizes addressing high-risk elements early to reduce project uncertainty and potential failures.

questions.question: A company routes only 5% of user traffic to a new release to detect problems before rolling it out to everyone. What deployment technique is this?
questions.explanation: Canary deployments expose a new version to a small subset of users first, limiting blast radius before full rollout.

questions.question: An e-commerce site keeps two identical production environments and instantly switches all traffic to the updated one after verification. What deployment technique is this?
questions.explanation: Blue-green deployment maintains two identical environments so traffic can switch instantly, enabling near-zero downtime and easy rollback.

questions.question: The four phases of the Rational Unified Process, in order.
questions.explanation: RUP divides each project into Inception, Elaboration, Construction, and Transition phases, each possibly spanning several iterations.

questions.question: The software engineer who proposed the Spiral model in 1988.
questions.explanation: Barry Boehm published 'A Spiral Model of Software Development and Enhancement' in 1988, introducing risk-driven iteration.

questions.question: The ISO/IEC standard that establishes a common framework for software life cycle processes.
questions.explanation: ISO/IEC 12207 (now ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207) defines the processes, activities, and tasks applicable during software acquisition, development, and maintenance.

questions.question: In the V-Model, the development phase during which integration test plans are prepared.
questions.explanation: Each V-Model development stage pairs with a test stage: high-level/architecture design pairs with integration testing (as system design pairs with system testing).

questions.question: In Boehm's Spiral model, the activity performed in each loop's second quadrant, right after objectives and alternatives are set.
questions.explanation: Quadrant 2 evaluates alternatives and identifies/resolves risks - typically through prototyping - before development proceeds.

questions.question: The Rational Unified Process phase whose milestone is 'Initial Operational Capability' - the first usable, beta-quality release of the system.
questions.explanation: In RUP, Construction builds out the remaining features and ends at the Initial Operational Capability milestone, before Transition deploys the product.

questions.question: In the V-Model, the development phase during which system test plans are prepared.
questions.explanation: System tests validate the overall system specification, so their plans are written in parallel with the system design stage on the V's left arm.

questions.question: The four quadrants of each loop in Boehm's Spiral model, in order.
questions.answer: Determine objectives and alternatives -> identify and resolve risks -> develop and verify the next-level product -> plan the next iteration
alternatives: 1) objectives & alternatives 2) risk resolution 3) develop & test 4) plan next loop
questions.explanation: Each spiral cycle sets objectives/alternatives, analyzes and resolves risks, develops and verifies that increment, then plans the next loop.
